messages.subject: Interpreting the lavaan output
parts:
I have analyzed my data which, were collected from a survey, using lavaan in R. I have some questions regarding the output?

1) My Chi-Square p value is 0.000<0.05. Does that mean my model cannot be used for estimation?

2) Do p-values corresponding to the indicators less than 0.05 mean that this indicator has statistically significant influence on the indicators' latent variable?

3) I noticed that my estimates are quite large compared to those I saw on the internet. Is that OK?

2) Do estimates of the indicators (S2, S3, etc) show how much they contribute to the relevant latent variable? For example, for latent variable "tech_etmeme", S4 has the greatest value (47.869). Does that mean, it has the greatest influence on "tech_etmeme"?

Here is my R code for my model:

model <- ' trch_etmeme  =~ S2 + S3 + S4 + S5 + S6 
              trch_etme =~ S7 + S8 + S9 + S10 + S11 
              dntl_implnt_scm_ndn  =~ S12 + S13 + S14 + S15 + S16
              hkm_trch_ndn =~ S17 + S18 + S19 + S20 + S21
              hstne_trch_ndn =~ S22 + S23 + S24 + S25 '

fit <- cfa(model,data = a,std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fit,standardized=TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
